NC_GLOBAL.title: FRF 17m Datawell Waverider Buoy
NC_GLOBAL.summary:
USACE/COAB data collected by a Datawell Directional Waverider (Mk III) approximately 2 miles (3.2 km) 
 offshore of Duck (FRF), NC.  The nominal depth for each deployment was approximately 17m NAVD88. 
 The original data processing was from timeseries the buoy transmitted via HF radio.  Heave-North-West
 buoy displacements were transmitted at 1.28 Hz.  Spectra and cross-spectra were computed and directional
 Fourier coefficients were computed (e.g., M.D. Earle, K.E. Steele, and D.W.C. Wang - Use of advanced 
 directional wave spectra analysis methods, Ocean Engineering 26 (1999) 1421\x131434).  That analysis was 
 done with data from Feb 1997 to May 2005. Between May 2005 and May 2013 directional Fourier coefficients (AB)
 were extracted from the HF data that the buoy computes onboard.  Directional spectra were computed from the 
 Fourier coefficients computed onboard the buoy.  Since May 2013 buoy was provided through the Coastal 
 Data Information Program (CDIP), UCSD San Diego, CA.  Data are transmitted via an Iridium satellite link 
 at half-hour intervals, with raw data record lengths of 30 minutes.  These data also provide the buoy computed
 Fourier coefficients but have been rotated from magnetic north to clockwise from true north.  
 Two dimensional (2D) frequency-direction spectra are computed using an Iterative Maximum Likelihood Estimator
 (IMLE) method.  See - Oltman-Shay, J., Guza, R.T., 1984. A data-adaptive ocean wave directional-spectrum 
 estimator for pitch and roll type measurements. Journal of Physical Oceanography 14, 1800\x131810.

 This buoy has other identifiers; 433 (CDIP), 630 (FRF), and 44056 (NDBC).

NC_GLOBAL.title: FRF 11m AWAC Waves
NC_GLOBAL.summary: USACE/COAB data collected by a bottom mounted (looking up) Nortek AWAC, approximately 1150m offshore  of Duck (FRF), NC at a nominal depth of 11m NAVD88.  Directional spectra are computed using a custom  COAB analysis of merging low frequency AST-UV (or PUV) spectra with high-end beam-array spectra  (see http link frf.usace.army.mil/realtime/awac/COAB_awacSpectralAnalysis.pdf).  Data collection is  hard-wired and analyzed hourly with 34 minute timeseries records.  Two dimensional frequency-direction  spectra are computed using a Maximum Likelihood Estimator (MLE) method.  The Fourier coefficients  were estimated from the 2D spectra.  A description of computing these coefficients is provided in Use of advanced directional wave spectra analysis methods, M. D. Earle, K. E. Steele, and D. W. C. Wang,  Ocean Engineering, Volume 26, Issue 12, December 1999, Pages 1421-1434. Or Kuik et. al, JPO, 18,  pp. 1020-1034, 1988.

NC_GLOBAL.title: FRF 8m Array
NC_GLOBAL.summary:
USACE Coastal Observation and Analysis Branch (COAB) collected directional wave data using 
 an array of pressure sensors at the Field Research Facility (FRF) in Duck, NC.  The array
 consists of 15 pressure gauges mounted approximately 0.5 m (1.6 ft) off the bottom in the 
 vicinity of the 8-m (26-ft) isobath about 900 m (2,953 ft) offshore and to the north of the 
 research pier.  Directional information is computed from these gauges using an iterative 
 maximum likelihood estimator.

 The location satisfies three constraints. First, it is generally outside the surf zone 
 so that linear wave theory is applicable in data processing. Second, it is in water shallow 
 enough that signals from 3-sec waves, the shortest periods of interest here, are detectable 
 above background noise at the bottom-mounted gauges. Third, it is located away from the 
 irregular isobaths around the pier and in the nearshore bar system, which helps minimize 
 bathymetrically induced inhomogeneities in the wave field.  The location of sensor 111 
 is selected as the nominal coordinate for this 120x255m array. 

 Spacing between gauges in the array appears irregular in the figure but, for the most part, 
 corresponds to the array-design criterion posed by Davis and Regier (1977) that every gauge 
 pair has a unique separation. The array geometry encompasses considerable ranges in both 
 sizes and numbers of gauge separations. Minimum gauge spacing is 5 m (16.4 ft) in both the 
 alongshore and cross-shore directions. Maximum spacing is 255 m (837 ft) in the alongshore 
 direction and 120 m (394 ft) in the cross-shore direction. Intermediate gauge spacings are 
 in multiples of5 m (16.4 ft). With 15 gauges, there are 105 possible unique spacings. In 
 the FRF array, 12 redundant spacings are intentionally left for ancillary examination of 
 spacial homogeneity of the wave field, so that 93 unique spacings remain. 

 Each pressure gauge is a Senso-Metric Model SP973(C), in which a piezoelectric strain gauge 
 detects displacement of a pressure-sensitive diaphragm referenced to an evacuated cavity. 
 Site calibrations indicate an accuracy of the pressure equivalent of 0.006 m (0.02 ft) of 
 water for wave-induced fluctuations about a static water column height of 8 m (26 ft). 
 Voltage analogs of pressure signals are hard-wired through 10-Hz, fourth-order, Butterworth 
 filters (primarily to eliminate 60-Hz noise) to an analog-to-digital signal converter.
 Discretization of the full-scale signal to 16-bit binary form results in a digitization 
 step of the equivalent of 0.0005 m (0.002 ft) of water, exceeding the accuracy of the 
 Senso-Metric gauges.

 bands;

 Freq (f, Hz)                Gauges Used (if passed QC tests)
  0.04 <= f < 0.07   [191 181 171 111 121 251 241 131 231 221 211 151 161]
  0.07 <= f < 0.11   [171 111 101 121 251 241 131 231 221 141 151 161]

 Wave frequency and direction bins have been interpolated to 0.01 Hz and 5 degrees from 
 the original analysis. This was done to maintain compatibility with other FRF directional 
wave data sets. 
***** Wave directions are coming from, degrees clockwise from true north (TN). *****


 Quality Control flag (qcFlag)-
 QC analysis follows the guidance in the NOAA IOOS manual for Real-Time Quality Control of
 In Situ Surface Wave Data, A Guide to Quality Control and Quality Assurance of In Situ 
 Surface Wave Observations, Version 2.0, August 2015. This document was developed in NOAA's 
 Quality Assurance of Real-Time Oceanographic Data (QARTOD) program.

 The qcFlags has the following values:
   1 = Checked - OK with automated realtime QC
   2 = Not checked
   3 = Questionable
   4 = Failed
   5 = Human checked/validated
  -9 = Missing data, used as a place holder

 There are separate qcFlags for the 1D and 2D spectra.  The qcflag_spec1D is considered the primary
 flag since if the 1D energy spectrum is bad then the 2D direction spectrum would also be bad.  There
 are occasions when the directional analysis did not obtain a reliable solution and the secondary
 qcFlag_spec2D flag is set.

 An additional flag (qcBitflag) contains additional information that may be useful for 
 interpreting the questionable or failed qcFlags.  This is stored as a 4-byte integer with bits 
 set (to 1) for various QC tests.  

 For the 8m-Array each sensor had its own bitFlag in the analysis.  If a sensor failed the QC
 tests it was dropped in the analysis.  The bitFlag with this data set is used to indicate if 
 the number of gauges dropped made the directional estimate questionable or failed.

 The qcBitflag bit numbers, LSB=1, MSB=16, if set to 1 == problem:
 1 = suspect wave height
 2 = failed wave height, out of range 
 3 = suspect wave period
 4 = failed wave period, out of range 
 5 = suspect wave direction out of range (alongshore)
 6 = failed wave direction out of range (from shore)
 7 = suspect low signal to noise ratio (SNR), mean of all used gauges  
 8 = failed low signal to noise ratio (SNR), mean of all used gauges
 9 = suspect high energy at low frequencies, mean of all used gauges
10 = failed, excessive high energy at low frequencies, mean of all used gauges 17 = directional estimate for freq-band 1 questionable 18 = directional estimate for freq-band 2 questionable 19 = directional estimate for freq-band 3 questionable 20 = directional estimate for freq-band 4 questionable 21 = directional estimate for freq-band 5 questionable 22 = directional estimate for freq-band 1 failed (10^-6 energy density filled)   23 = directional estimate for freq-band 2 failed (10^-6 energy density filled)   24 - directional estimate for freq-band 3 failed (10^-6 energy density filled)   25 = directional estimate for freq-band 4 failed (10^-6 energy density filled)   26 = directional estimate for freq-band 5 failed (10^-6 energy density filled)  

 Directional estimates would be flagged questionable if only 3 sensors (minimal but possibly OK) 
 were used in that frequency band. If less than half the gauges are used for the first 3 (of 5)
 frequency bands and Directional estimates are flagged failed when less than 3 
 gauges were available.

NC_GLOBAL.title: FRF 26m Datawell Waverider Buoy
NC_GLOBAL.summary:
USACE/COAB collected directional wave data with a Datawell Directional Waverider (Mk III) approximately 
 10 miles (16.1 km) offshore of Duck (FRF), NC. The nominal depth for each deployment was approximately 
 26m NAVD88. Directional spectra Fourier coefficients are computed onboard the buoy and transmitted via 
 Iridium satellite link at half-hour intervals, raw data record lengths are 30 minutes. The USACE funds this
 data collection through the Coastal Data Information Program (CDIP), UCSD San Diego, CA.  The buoy computed 
 Directional Fourier coefficients are provided but have been rotated from magnetic north to clockwise from 
 true north.  Two dimensional (2D) frequency-direction spectra are computed using an Maximum Likelihood Estimator
 (MLE) method.  See - Oltman-Shay, J., Guza, R.T., 1984. A data-adaptive ocean wave directional-spectrum 
 estimator for pitch and roll type measurements. Journal of Physical Oceanography 14, 1800–1810. 
 This buoy has other identifiers; 44100 at the National Data Buoy Center (NDBC), 430 at CDIP and the FRF.

NC_GLOBAL.title: FRF 11m AWAC Currents
NC_GLOBAL.summary:
USACE/COAB data collected by a bottom mounted (looking up) Nortek AWAC, approximately 1150m offshore of Duck (FRF), NC 
  at a nominal depth of -11m NAVD 88.  Directional current profiles were interpolated to 0.5m intervals relative to 
  NAVD88, and depth integrated currents are computed.  Data values start closest to the gauge and go upwards.
  This instrument is hard-wired to a shore-based data acquisition system and analyzed on one or two hour intervals.  
  Directions are flowing towards clockwise fron true north (0 degrees is flowing towards true north, 90 degrees to the east). 
  These data have been processed and QC checked with an automated analysis progran and should be considered preliminary.
